checks.name: Empty bodies are rejected before worker creation
The 64 MiB allocation cap is enforced before admission
An empty writer window is rejected
A missing writer cannot retain a budget lease
A received tail waits in memory and earns no disk resume credit across a gap
Finishing with a gap never writes the tail or claims a complete body
Buffered-only bytes cannot supply a completion body or saved segment prefix
Closed generations reject further input
A second close cannot change an already settled policy or issue new IO
Out-of-order network input completes only after every ordered write is acknowledged
The writer emits contiguous ascending windows with the exact original bytes
Resume credit is clipped to the requested valid segment
Only a settled successful finish exposes the full cached body
Pause drains accepted noncontiguous spans without declaring completion
Pause credit cannot cross a missing segment prefix
Paused tail data is preserved while completion exposure remains closed
Abort discards buffered-only tails without granting saved progress
A held storage operation is observable without locking out state readers
Identical retries do not overwrite in-flight bytes or credit a held write
Conflicting retries are rejected before modifying accepted data
Identical retries neither duplicate writes nor change the completed representation
A failed write never earns completion or resume credit
Storage failure closes completion and propagates to later producers
A later partial write preserves earlier credit but grants none for the failed operation
Physically changed but unacknowledged bytes cannot imply completeness
Eight producers share one stable buffer and preserve exact ordered output
Out-of-range and overflowing offsets cannot alter buffer state
Oversized and missing-source writes are rejected before copying
A valid zero-length notification accepts no bytes
A second experimental body allocation is refused while the first lease is live
Closing retains ownership while the body storage remains alive
A successor acquires the budget after the prior buffer is destroyed
Excessive fragmented metadata is rejected atomically at its fixed limit
Metadata refusal preserves prior accepted bytes without false credit
Abort control holds a real in-flight writer callback
Abort closes producer admission before joining the active operation
Abort acknowledges an operation that already succeeded and starts no later writes
A writer callback cannot close and join its own thread
A real regular file receives no tail write across a gap
Real positioned writes advance from zero without gaps or reordered IO
A separate explicit final flush remains the caller's responsibility
The flushed regular file preserves every original byte after tail-first admission
A real paused file retains only its acknowledged segment-prefix credit
The paused output contains the exact tail while its unwritten leading gap remains uncredited
A fully written paused body cannot be exported as confirmed completion
An abort cannot export completion even when all writes already succeeded
A failed writer cannot hand storage to the completion-hash stage
